data.title: Nvidia sinks roughly 40% as AI bubble fears drag Bitcoin below $60,000
data.description:
The AI trade is having its worst stretch yet. Nvidia shares have fallen roughly 40% in a matter of weeks, and the damage has spread well past Silicon Valley.

Bitcoin has slipped below $60,000. The total crypto market has contracted to approximately $2 trillion. When the poster child of a boom stumbles this hard, almost everything with a risk label feels it.

Nvidia closed at an all-time high of $243.37 on October 6, 2026. By mid-November, the stock was trading around $150.

That is a decline of about 40% from peak to trough. For a company that spent the past few years as the market's favorite growth story, the reversal has been swift.

The pain has not stayed confined to one ticker. The S&P 500 has entered correction territory, with weekly losses exceeding 8% as of November 21, 2026.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average has also slipped into a correction. Both benchmarks now sit more than 10% below their recent peaks.

At the center of the anxiety is a single question. Investors are asking whether the trillions of dollars flowing into AI infrastructure will ever earn back what they cost.

The numbers driving the worry are stark. AI infrastructure spending is projected at $7 trillion through 2030.

Gartner, the research firm, forecasts AI revenue over the same window at only $3.6 trillion. Put those two figures side by side and the gap is hard to ignore.

Nvidia sells the picks and shovels of the AI gold rush, mainly the chips that power data centers. If the companies buying those chips start doubting the payoff, they may slow their orders.

Bitcoin traded below $60,000 on November 21, 2026, with an intraday low somewhere between $55,000 and $57,000. The asset has now fallen more than 30% since September 2026.

The wider crypto market has fared no better. Total crypto market capitalization has shrunk to approximately $2 trillion, down from a peak above $4 trillion in October 2025.

The selling pressure on Bitcoin appears to reflect a broad, macro-driven liquidity squeeze rather than any problem specific to crypto. No major exchange failure or protocol exploit is behind this move.

Instead, Bitcoin is trading like what it has increasingly become: a high-beta risk asset that moves with tech stocks. When investors pull money out of speculative growth bets, digital assets tend to get swept up in the same tide.

The first takeaway is that the AI story and the crypto story are more tightly linked than many holders would like. A correction triggered by doubts over data center spending has knocked Bitcoin down by more than 30%.

Third, the gap between projected AI spending and forecast revenue is unlikely to close quickly. A $7 trillion capex bill against $3.6 trillion in expected revenue is a structural mismatch, not a quarterly blip. Each new earnings report from chipmakers and cloud providers will be read as evidence for or against the bubble thesis.

For crypto traders, the key signal may sit outside crypto entirely. As long as Bitcoin trades in step with the Nasdaq and the S&P 500, the path of the AI trade could help set the direction for digital assets too.

data.title: Lufthansa To Cut 1,000 Jobs At Flagship Airline
data.description:
Rising fuel costs, strike-related expenses and mounting losses have prompted the German airline to intensify its restructuring efforts

German airline Lufthansa plans to eliminate 1,000 full-time positions at its flagship airline, Lufthansa Airlines, as mounting financial pressures and rising operating costs force the company to accelerate its restructuring efforts.

The proposed job cuts will affect operations at the airline's Frankfurt and Munich hubs and represent approximately 2.5 per cent of its workforce of around 40,000 employees. The announcement was communicated to employees through an internal letter signed by Lufthansa Airlines chief executive Jens Ritter and other senior executives.

The management attributed the decision to the airline's deteriorating financial position, citing persistently high fuel prices, strike-related expenses and an already elevated cost base. The company said its earlier turnaround measures were no longer sufficient to secure its long-term financial stability.

During the first nine months of 2026, Lufthansa Airlines recorded an operating loss of approximately €180 million, translating into average monthly losses of around €20 million.

The internal communication also highlighted the impact of the conflict in the Middle East, which has contributed to higher fuel costs, alongside nine days of strike action during the year. Management said these developments had further intensified the airline's operational and financial challenges.

The workforce reduction forms part of a broader efficiency drive that will also involve changes to the airline's flight operations and fleet strategy. Lufthansa plans to further reduce capacity on short and medium-haul routes and reduce the number of Airbus A320-family aircraft in its fleet, partially replacing them with smaller and more fuel-efficient Airbus A220 aircraft.

The airline is also accelerating the installation of Starlink satellite-based internet connectivity across its fleet, aiming to generate additional revenue through onboard connectivity services.

The latest announcement follows Lufthansa Group's September 2025 plan to eliminate approximately 4,000 administrative positions by 2030, primarily through digitalisation and the consolidation of administrative functions. However, it remains unclear whether the newly announced 1,000 job reductions at Lufthansa Airlines are included in that earlier target or represent additional cuts.

The restructuring comes amid wider challenges for the European aviation industry, particularly from volatile fuel prices, labour disputes and increasing pressure to improve operational efficiency. Lufthansa has also been engaged in negotiations with pilot unions over pay and working conditions, with disagreements continuing over proposed employment terms.

Interestingly, the financial performance of the wider Lufthansa Group has been relatively stronger than that of its flagship airline. The group reported a 30 per cent increase in net profit during the July-September quarter, supported by demand for premium long-haul travel. However, the core Lufthansa Airlines business continues to face profitability challenges.

At the end of 2025, Lufthansa Group employed 103,255 people worldwide, with approximately 64 per cent working across its passenger airlines. The latest restructuring highlights the distinction between the group's overall financial performance and the continuing pressure on its flagship carrier to improve productivity, control costs and restore profitability.

data.title: Broadcom AI outlook in focus beyond quarterly results, Goldman says
data.description:
For Broadcom , the focus would likely be beyond its quarterly results and on whether demand for AI chips can remain strong through 2028, as per Goldman Sachs analysts."We expect modest upside to guidance, but believe the stock will ultimately be driven more by clarity on the sustainability of AI spending into 2028, and Broadcom’s competitive position at key accounts such as Google," analysts at Goldman Sachs said.

AVGO stock was down 10% on Friday trading after a report revealed Google ()() is cutting planned shipments of its Broadcom-designed AI chips for 2027, while increasing orders for chips designed by MediaTek.

Concerns are growing about shortages of land, electricity, and buildings needed to house large-scale data centers. There are also questions about whether smaller cloud providers focused on AI will be able to secure enough outside funding to support their expansion. These emerging cloud providers account for about 6.3 gigawatts of Broadcom's planned 10 gigawatts of custom AI chip deployments in 2027. In 2028 emerging cloud providers are expected to account for about 75% of Broadcom's planned custom AI chip deployments.

Broadcom's competitive position is also at focus, especially after stock lost more than 10% value on Friday following reports of Google cutting Broadcom-designed AI chips while increasing orders for chips designed by MediaTek.

"We believe incremental detail on the durability of key customer engagements for next-generation XPUs as competitive intensity increases from providers such as MediaTek, could be impactful for the stock," Goldman analysts said.

Goldman cut the price target on Broadcom to $460 from $540, as it reduced the valuation multiple it applies to the company's expected earnings, from 30 times to 25 times.

Broadcom will report its fourth quarter results on December 9.

data.title: Bitcoin drops to lowest level in more than two years
data.description:

Bitcoin’s selloff has coincided with a broader decline in the tech sector as investors review their investments in riskier assets amid fears over another Federal Reserve rate hike next month.

The abrupt resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, Anthropic’s record-breaking IPO, and increasing regulatory risks for the cryptocurrency industry following the Democrats’ ​victory ⁠in the midterm elections have added another dimension to the bitcoin’s valuation debate.

data.title: BlackRock's IBIT posts record $541M outflow as Bitcoin ETFs bleed $3.47B in November
data.description:
BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) just had the worst day in its history. On November 19, 2026, the fund recorded a net outflow of $541.1 million, its largest single-day redemption since launching in January 2024.

It wasn't an isolated bad afternoon, either. US spot Bitcoin ETFs have now shed approximately $3.47 billion in net outflows so far in November, and IBIT is doing most of the heavy lifting on the way out.

IBIT's $541.1 million exit topped its previous worst day: a $528.3 million outflow on January 30, 2026. That earlier record lasted less than a year.

Across all US spot Bitcoin ETFs, net outflows on November 19 totaled $582.3 million. That marked three consecutive days of redemptions for the group.

IBIT accounted for roughly 93% of that daily total. The concentration holds up over the full month too. BlackRock's fund represents about 85% of November's cumulative ETF outflows so far.

Other issuers felt the pressure, just on a smaller scale. Fidelity's FBTC lost $45.9 million on the day, while ARK 21Shares' ARKB saw $31.3 million leave.

One fund went the other way. Morgan Stanley's MSBT pulled in $49.6 million of fresh inflows on the same day, making it the rare product with money arriving rather than leaving.

The redemptions landed alongside a sharp slide in the underlying asset. Bitcoin traded around $61,800 to $62,000 on November 19, after falling below the $62,000 mark.

The price dropped about 3% over 24 hours and nearly 10% across the preceding week. That left Bitcoin at its weakest level since early July 2026.

The research behind this story ties the slide to macroeconomic pressure, including rising Treasury yields and shifting expectations around the Federal Reserve.

For all the red ink, the spot Bitcoin ETF complex remains large. The 12 US spot Bitcoin ETFs held approximately $76.6 billion in assets as of November 19.

That figure represents about 6.1% of Bitcoin's total market capitalization. Since their January 2024 debut, the funds have attracted around $53.5 billion in cumulative net inflows. Against that backdrop, approximately $3.47 billion in November outflows is a notable dent, though not a demolition.

The most striking detail is how concentrated the selling has been. When one fund accounts for roughly 93% of a day's outflows, the story is partly about Bitcoin and partly about who holds IBIT.

The MSBT inflow complicates any simple narrative of uniform panic. Some allocators were apparently still willing to add Bitcoin exposure on the same day others were trimming it.

For traders, ETF flow data has become one of the clearest windows into institutional and advisor-driven demand. Persistent outflows can add selling pressure to the spot market, since redemptions typically require funds to reduce their Bitcoin holdings.

data.title: Tentative Deal Averts Strike Threat at Busiest U.S. Ports — WSJ
data.description:
By Paul Berger

Port employers in Southern California and unionized security guards reached a tentative labor deal, averting a strike threat at the nation's busiest container-handling complex as retailers rush in last-minute holiday items.

The Pacific Maritime Association said early Saturday the current labor contract with 250 guards at the ports of Los Angeles and Long Beach would be extended pending ratification of the tentative deal by the workers.

The contract with the local chapter of the International Longshore and Warehouse Union had been due to expire at 12:01 a.m. Saturday and the guards had already voted to authorize a strike. Although the guards account for just 2% of the ports' unionized workforce, other ILWU dockworkers were expected to refuse to cross picket lines.

"This agreement provides certainty for the ports, for the cargo owners and workers throughout the supply chain who depend on them, and for the Southern California, regional and national economies," the employers said in a statement.

Union representatives didn't immediately respond to a request for comment.

The Southern California ports have been deluged with cargo this fall. In October, the ports moved a combined more than 1 million loaded import boxes, measured in 20-foot-equivalent units, for the second month in a row as the traditional peak shipping season extended into the final quarter of the year.

Shipping industry officials had warned that a strike would affect six of the ports' 13 container-handling terminals, accounting for more than half of the gateway's cargo.

Port employers warned this week of growing potential for a strike because of a lack of progress in labor talks. The maritime association said earlier this week that its contract offer included a pay increase that would lift average full-time wages to $198,000 from more than $170,000.

The employers didn't provide details of the wage offer in the tentative deal.

data.title: Generali Central Life Insurance Takes ‘Bada Socho’ Campaign To Consumers Through Interactive Dreams Wall
data.description:
The latest phase of ‘HERE.NOW.’ combines a digital pledge platform with a large-scale public activation in Mumbai and a multi-channel media strategy

Generali Central Life Insurance (GCLI) has expanded its national brand campaign, ‘HERE.NOW.’, with the launch of the Bada Socho Dreams Wall, an interactive digital initiative that invites people to share their aspirations and commit to one meaningful step towards achieving them.

Hosted on the company’s website, the Dreams Wall encourages individuals to put their dreams into words and turn them into actionable commitments. The initiative builds on the brand’s ‘Bada Socho’ philosophy, positioning life insurance as a means of supporting aspirations and long-term goals.

The latest phase follows two earlier chapters of ‘HERE.NOW.’, which was launched in November 2025 after the company’s rebranding and the entry of Central Bank of India as its joint venture partner. The first phase focused on new beginnings and significant life milestones. In February 2026, the campaign moved to the aspirations of Indian families, highlighting the importance of securing a child’s future and planning for retirement.

The current chapter shifts the focus from dreaming to taking action. Through its message, ‘Bada Socho for your bindass dreams’, the campaign encourages consumers to make meaningful decisions in the present to build the future they envision.

To extend its reach across the country, GCLI has rolled out a Bharat-focused media strategy spanning television, cricket, outdoor, transit media, connected TV, OTT and digital platforms. Its media associations include the India tour of Sri Lanka, India Ke Top 1% on Star Plus, Bigg Boss on Star Maa and Star Vijay, Sa Re Ga Ma Pa on Zee Telugu and Zee Keralam, and Dance Karnataka Dance on Zee Kannada.

The campaign also includes placements across news and general entertainment channels, Delhi Metro advertising, connected TV and OTT platforms such as JioHotstar and Sony LIV, along with social media amplification. Outdoor visibility across more than 100 cities in 10 languages forms part of the effort to reach consumers across regions and demographic groups.

Taking the campaign beyond digital and traditional media, the company has also introduced the Bada Socho Cube, a large-scale Rubik’s Cube installation at Mumbai’s Carter Road promenade. The public activation was preceded by a mystery gift box installation, building anticipation before the Cube’s reveal. The installation translates the campaign’s message into an interactive experience, highlighting how everyday choices can contribute to larger aspirations.

Geetanjali Chugh Kothari, Chief Marketing Officer, Generali Central Life Insurance, says, “Over the last year, HERE.NOW. has evolved into a platform that encourages Indians to dream bigger about their future and take meaningful steps towards it. With this initiative, we wanted to transform inspiration into action through the Bada Socho Dreams Wall. We believe that when people write down their dreams, aspirations become more tangible and achievable. By inviting Indians to publicly pledge one meaningful step towards their goals, we hope to inspire a movement that encourages action, accountability and future readiness. At Generali Central Life Insurance, we remain committed to empowering people to think bigger, dream boldly and act HERE.NOW. for the future they envision.”

According to the company, the first two phases of ‘HERE.NOW.’ reached more than 65 million consumers, generated over 140 million impressions across television, cricket and outdoor media, and recorded more than 150 million digital views. The latest phase aims to build on this reach by bringing consumers into the campaign through participation and personal commitments.

EE News Desk

data.title: Noel Tata Renews Demand For Tata Sons Board Recordings
data.description:
In his third request for the September 17 meeting's recordings, the Tata Trusts chairman has sought unedited audio and video files, final minutes and details of changes made to the meeting agenda ahead of the November 26 board meeting

Tata Trusts chairman Noel Tata has renewed his demand for the audio and video recordings of a crucial Tata Sons board meeting, while questioning the procedure through which N Chandrasekaran was reappointed as chairman for another five-year term.

In a letter sent on Friday to Tata Sons company secretary Suprakash Mukhopadhyay, Noel sought complete and unedited recordings of the 17 September board meeting, along with any transcripts and confirmation that the original files and their metadata had been preserved.

He also sought the final signed minutes of the meeting or, if they remain unsigned, a revised draft indicating which of his proposed corrections had been accepted and recording his dissent where they had not. Noel has sought a response by 25 November, a day before the next Tata Sons board meeting scheduled for 26 November, according to media reports.

The latest communication marks Noel's third request for the recordings. Tata Sons had declined his earlier demand, maintaining that neither the law nor the company's Articles of Association required it to retain or share recordings of in-person board meetings with directors.

Dispute Over Reappointment

Noel has questioned the legal and procedural basis for Chandrasekaran's reappointment, arguing that the decision was not included as a specific item on the 17  September meeting agenda.

According to his objections, the agenda referred to a debrief from the company's Nomination and Remuneration Committee (NRC), rather than a formal recommendation to reappoint Chandrasekaran. The committee had met on 3 September and asked him to reconsider his decision to step down, but had not formally recommended his reappointment, Noel has argued.

He has also questioned the legal basis for the resolution, including the relevant provisions of Tata Sons' Articles of Association and the requirement for shareholder approval at a valid annual general meeting.

At the 17 September meeting, Noel opposed Chandrasekaran's reappointment, while Tata Trusts nominee director Venu Srinivasan supported it. Noel subsequently walked out of the meeting.

Tata Sons' Earlier Response

In its 9 November response to Noel's earlier requests, Tata Sons said audio and video recording of board proceedings was required only when one or more directors attended a meeting remotely. It said recordings of in-person meetings were used to help the company secretary prepare draft minutes and did not need to be retained or shared with directors.

The company also said the draft minutes of the 17 September meeting had been uploaded to its board application on 1 October and that it had received Noel's comments on 8 October. Changes considered appropriate had been incorporated, and the revised minutes would be placed before the board for confirmation.

Noel's latest letter also seeks the formal meeting notice, successive versions of the agenda, details of when and by whom changes were made, and an audit trail of documents uploaded to the board's web application.

He has additionally raised questions about business dealings involving Hanno One Warehousing, whose directors include members of Chandrasekaran's family, and its reported commercial relationship with TVS Motor. Tata Sons has previously rejected allegations of a conflict of interest involving the relationship, maintaining that the relevant disclosures were made.

The renewed correspondence comes amid wider differences between Noel Tata and other Tata Sons directors over the group's ownership structure, regulatory obligations and the proposed listing of the holding company.

data.title: Port Cargo Traffic Jumps 18.7% In October As EXIM Trade Surges
data.description:
Record coastal shipments, stronger capital goods movement and increased container handling support activity across major and minor ports

India’s port cargo movement accelerated in October, supported by stronger export-import activity, higher coastal shipments and increased movement of engineering and electronic goods. Aggregate cargo volumes across major and minor ports rose 18.7 per cent year-on-year, compared with 6.3 per cent growth recorded in September, according to a research report by JM Financial.

The improvement in port activity coincided with a 32.7 per cent increase in core export-import (EXIM) trade during the month. The brokerage attributed the growth to higher imports and exports of engineering and electronic products, alongside increased movement of capital goods across international markets.

Capital goods trade recorded particularly strong growth, with imports rising 36 per cent year-on-year and exports increasing 44 per cent in October. Core exports, excluding petroleum products, gold, silver and precious metals, grew 33.5 per cent, while core imports registered a 32.1 per cent increase during the month.

Major ports handled 93.6 million metric tonnes (mmt) of cargo in October, registering 22.5 per cent year-on-year growth. Coastal cargo accounted for a significant share of the increase, reaching a record 31.6 mmt during the month, up 80.8 per cent from the corresponding period last year.

Across major and minor ports, coastal cargo volumes increased 50.9 per cent year-on-year, while overseas cargo movement grew 10.1 per cent. The brokerage said the sharp increase in coastal shipments was the primary driver of the improvement in aggregate cargo volumes during October.

Minor ports handled 68.4 mmt of cargo, marking 13.8 per cent year-on-year growth. Higher shipments of petroleum, oil and lubricants (POL) and coal supported the increase, reflecting stronger movement across key commodity segments.

Container Volumes Show Divergence

Container activity also recorded strong growth during October, with aggregate container volumes increasing 26.8 per cent year-on-year. However, container tonnage rose by only 11.8 per cent, indicating that the increase in container handling was not matched by a proportionate rise in the weight of cargo transported.

JM Financial attributed this divergence to higher transhipment activity, wherein containers are transferred between vessels at intermediate ports before reaching their final destinations. The brokerage also highlighted the gap between EXIM trade growth and cargo tonnage, pointing to changing patterns in trade and cargo composition.

Core EXIM trade expanded 32.7 per cent during October, significantly higher than the 11.8 per cent growth in aggregate container tonnage and 22.5 per cent increase in major port cargo volumes. According to the brokerage, the divergence also indicates sharp price inflation, particularly in engineering and electronic goods.

Coal And Iron Ore Rise

Bulk commodity movement remained positive during October, with coal and iron ore shipments recording year-on-year growth across major and minor ports. Coal volumes increased 15.2 per cent to 37.5 mmt, while aggregate iron ore cargo rose 7.8 per cent to 9.4 mmt during the month.

The increase in commodity shipments, alongside stronger coastal and container activity, points to broader growth in port operations. Higher movement of industrial goods and capital equipment also contributed to the expansion in cargo volumes during the period.

JM Financial said strong external trade and rising movement of capital goods could continue to support port activity. However, the divergence between container volumes, cargo tonnage and EXIM trade growth highlights the impact of higher transhipment activity, changing cargo composition and inflationary pressures.

data.title: Global Oil Market Heads Towards Surplus, Crude Prices May Fall To $70 By 2027
data.description:
Higher output from non-OPEC+ producers and weaker Chinese consumption are expected to reshape global energy markets over coming quarters

Global crude oil prices could decline to around USD 70 per barrel by the end of 2027 as rising production outside the OPEC+ alliance and weakening Chinese demand push the market towards a supply surplus, according to a JM Financial report.

Brent crude is expected to remain elevated and volatile in the near term before moderating as global supply-demand conditions improve. The assessment is based on an expert session with Iman Nasseri, Senior Vice President for Middle East and Asia at FGE Nexant, which examined the outlook for crude oil, refined petroleum products and liquefied natural gas (LNG).

The global oil market is expected to move into a surplus as production growth outside OPEC+ increases while Chinese oil demand declines. The combination of higher supplies and weaker consumption could limit upward pressure on crude prices over the coming quarters, the report said.

The report also indicated that inventory restocking was unlikely to provide significant support to prices. China is expected to increase crude purchases gradually once prices fall below USD 70 per barrel, rather than aggressively building inventories.

Demand from the United States is also unlikely to provide additional support, as the current administration is not expected to replenish the country's Strategic Petroleum Reserve (SPR). These factors could further reduce the likelihood of a sustained rally in global crude prices.

Geopolitical Uncertainty Persists

Despite the improving supply outlook, geopolitical developments are expected to remain an important factor influencing crude prices in the near term. A US-Iran agreement is considered unlikely in the immediate future, although the possibility of a resolution could improve by mid-2027 as economic pressure on Iran increases.

Nasseri said an agreement would be difficult without a change in the political leadership of either country. He also highlighted the continued influence of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), which maintains strong control over Iran despite mounting economic pressure.

Meanwhile, crude flows through the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea have recovered to around 90 per cent of pre-war levels. The recovery has been supported by risk-tolerant vessels, exemptions for Iraqi and select Chinese cargoes, and transit payments made by Gulf countries for safe passage.

Refining Margins Remain Strong

While crude prices could moderate over the longer term, refining margins are expected to remain elevated in the near term because of supply constraints in diesel and other refined petroleum products. The report expects refining margins and product cracks to gradually normalise by the end of calendar year 2027.

Global refinery runs in October 2026 were around 5 million barrels per day below February levels, reflecting reduced operations across the Middle East, Russia and China. Lower refinery output has tightened the availability of refined products, particularly diesel, providing support to refining margins.

The report indicated that these supply constraints could persist even as the broader crude oil market moves towards a surplus. This could result in crude prices softening while refiners continue to benefit from relatively stronger product margins.

The global liquefied natural gas market is expected to remain tight through the 2026-27 winter, keeping prices elevated amid supply constraints. However, additional liquefaction capacity from the United States and Qatar could improve global availability from the second half of 2027.

The expected capacity additions could push the LNG market into a surplus, putting downward pressure on prices. Consequently, global LNG prices are likely to moderate from the second half of 2027, according to the report.

data.title: Ujjivan SFB CEO Seeks Early Exit, Furtado to Lead
data.description:
Ujjivan SFB CEO Sanjeev Nautiyal seeks early retirement on health grounds. Carol Furtado will take interim charge from September 1, 2026, subject to RBI approval

Ujjivan Small Finance Bank's Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer Sanjeev Nautiyal has sought early retirement on health grounds, prompting the lender's board to appoint Executive Director Carol Furtado as interim MD and CEO with effect from September 1, 2026. The Bengaluru-based lender said its board approved Nautiyal's request and appointed Furtado as acting MD and CEO on the recommendation of the Nomination and Remuneration Committee. Her appointment was subject to approval from the Reserve Bank of India (RBI).

Nautiyal's tenure was originally scheduled to end on November 30, 2026. He will remain on leave during his three-month notice period, beginning September 1, the bank said. Nautiyal served as the bank's MD and CEO for around two years. During his tenure, Ujjivan SFB strengthened its secured loan book and deposit franchise, while enhancing its digital and analytics capabilities, risk management practices and internal control framework.

Carol Furtado Takes Interim Charge

Furtado, who was serving as Executive Director at Ujjivan Small Finance Bank, brings more than three decades of experience across business, strategy, operations, people management and institutional functions. The bank said Furtado had been part of its leadership team and contributed to business growth, organisational transformation and development. Her appointment is intended to ensure continuity in the bank's leadership while the lender identifies a permanent successor to Nautiyal. The board will initiate the selection process and submit its recommendation to the RBI.

Bank Begins Search For Permanent Successor

The leadership transition comes as Ujjivan SFB works towards maintaining business continuity and strengthening its operating framework. The bank highlighted progress in secured lending, deposit mobilisation, digital capabilities and risk management during Nautiyal's tenure. The appointment of an interim chief executive will provide leadership support during the transition, while the process of appointing a regular MD and CEO remains subject to regulatory approval.

data.title: Bitcoin slips below its 200-week average for the first time since October 2023
data.description:
Bitcoin has fallen below its 200-week moving average for the first time since October 2023. That trendline has historically served as one of the market's sturdiest floors.

In mid-November 2026, the world's largest digital asset traded between $58,800 and $65,350. The 200-week average sits at roughly $68,000, putting the price somewhere between 5% and 13.7% beneath it.

Think of the 200-week moving average as Bitcoin's long-run center of gravity. It averages closing prices across nearly four years, which smooths out the daily drama into one slow-moving line.

Bitcoin has spent about 90% of its time above it. It has closed below the line in only about 9% to 11% of weeks since 2014.

The latest slide came alongside heavy selling in US spot Bitcoin ETFs. Net outflows topped $1.4 billion over recent sessions, with some tallies putting the November figure as high as $2 billion across multiple sessions.

Leverage made things worse. Liquidations of short-term positions have exceeded $1 billion since early November, as traders betting on higher prices were forcibly closed out. The Crypto Fear & Greed Index, a popular sentiment gauge, has sunk to extremely low levels.

Market maker Wintermute has warned that Bitcoin could come under further pressure and potentially slide into the $50,000s. The firm pointed to two drivers: fading ETF support and rising Treasury yields.

Analyst Benjamin Cowen has gone further. He suggested a target around $40,000 if current support levels fail to hold.

Analysts broadly agree on what would change the picture. They want clear signs of renewed ETF inflows, or stabilization above key price levels, before any bullish momentum can return.

Bitcoin has been here before. Past breaks below the 200-week average occurred in 2015, 2020, and 2022.

Following similar breaks, Bitcoin typically fell another 10% to 17% before recovering. The longer-term numbers are more flattering. Median one-year returns after these events exceeded 100%, and three-year gains topped 500%, according to the historical comparisons.

The longest stretch below the line came during the 2022-2023 bear market. Bitcoin stayed under it for 30 weeks.

For traders, the ETF flow data is likely the number to watch. The spot funds have become a primary channel for institutional money, and their outflows coincided closely with this decline.

Wintermute's mention of Treasury yields underscores how tightly Bitcoin is now tied to traditional finance. When government bonds pay more, the appeal of assets that pay nothing, like Bitcoin, tends to weaken.

For long-term investors, history suggests these breaks have rewarded patience over one-to-three-year horizons, but past performance is a guide, not a guarantee. The 10% to 17% further drawdowns that often followed earlier breaks are a reminder that buying the first crossing can still hurt.

data.title: 2,500 Bitcoin worth $147M moves from Kraken to an unknown wallet
data.description:
A wallet linked to Kraken sent 2,500 Bitcoin to an unidentified address, a transfer valued at approximately $147 million.

Whale Alert, the on-chain tracker that flags unusually large crypto movements, picked it up on November 19, 2026. The recipient has no public label, no known owner, and no stated purpose.

The basic facts are simple. Coins left an address associated with Kraken and landed in a wallet nobody has identified.

No public records name the owner of the receiving address. Nothing explains why it needed 2,500 BTC.

This was not a one-off. Kraken has posted several large outflows in recent days.

On November 18, 2026, a transfer of 2,789 BTC left the exchange. Two days earlier, on November 16, 2026, a 1,533 BTC withdrawal went out.

Exchanges often send funds through hot wallets before spreading them to final destinations. Previous Kraken transfers followed that pattern.

A hot wallet is connected to the internet and handles daily traffic, like a cash register. Cold storage is offline, closer to a bank vault.

The latest move also fits Kraken's historical transfer patterns. It happened while Bitcoin traded between $55,000 and $70,000 per coin.

Services like Whale Alert exist because big holders, or whales, can move markets. When thousands of BTC change hands, traders want to know first.

The logic runs both ways. Coins flowing into an exchange can hint that someone plans to sell. Coins flowing out can suggest a holder wants to sit tight.

The transaction itself only shows that coins moved from point A to point B. It does not confirm a sale, a change in custody, or any particular intent.

The unknown recipient is the open question here. Without a label, the address could belong to a client, an institution, or Kraken itself shuffling its own reserves.

One thing the current data does not support: any link to theft or forced liquidation. There is no verifiable information tying these specific transfers to either scenario.

The more plausible explanations are mundane. Treasury management and client withdrawals fit the evidence better than immediate selling pressure does.

There are a few things worth tracking from here. The first is whether the recipient address moves the coins again.

If the 2,500 BTC heads back to an exchange, that would change the story. Coins returning to a trading venue tend to raise sell-side questions that coins sitting still do not.

The second is whether the address ever gets a label. On-chain analysts often tie wallets to known entities over time.

The third is whether Kraken's outflow streak continues. Three big moves in four days could be a coincidence of timing, or part of a larger reshuffle.

For now, the transfer sits in the category of large but unexplained. That is a common category in crypto, where every transaction is public and almost no motive is.

data.title: EU leaders' chair proposes new cuts to EU 2028-2034 budget draft, suggests digital tax
data.description:
Key points:
  • Costa proposes 3% digital tax on online advertising and intermediation turnover
  • Proposal cuts seven-year EU budget by €40 billion to €1.582 trillion versus October draft
  • EU leaders discuss plan on November 26 to 27 aiming for December agreement

By Jan Strupczewski

The chairman of European Union leaders proposed further cuts to the European Commission's draft EU 2028-2034 budget on Saturday and suggested new revenue streams for the EU, including a digital tax, to help finance EU policies.

The cuts proposed by Antonio Costa, who chairs summits of EU leaders, would reduce the overall seven-year budget by €40 billion to €1.582 trillion compared to a proposal presented by the Irish EU presidency in October and by €180.6 billion compared to the original Commission proposal.

Costa's proposal mainly cuts the European Competitiveness Fund — aimed at helping make European industry more competitive against China and the United States — defence and external spending. Money for agriculture and cohesion is relatively protected compared to the Irish compromise proposal.

Nevertheless, France criticised the new numbers as not sufficiently protecting farmers, and the European Parliament's chief budget negotiator, Siegfried Muresan, said the numbers were a step backwards.

"This proposal is unacceptable to Parliament and cannot form the basis for our consent. The EU budget is an investment budget. Cuts, more cuts and a side of cuts are not an investment strategy," he said.

EU leaders will discuss Costa's proposals at a special summit on November 26-27 with a view to narrowing differences between the EU budget's net contributors and net beneficiaries, and to reaching an agreement in December.

The EU budget is how the 27-member bloc finances all its policies — from supporting farmers to developing new technology and supporting industry and research against competition from China and the US.

It also covers student exchanges, equalising standards of living across the EU, help for Ukraine and EU officials' salaries, among others.

DIGITAL TAX A PROPOSED NEW REVENUE

The EU budget is financed from national contributions and the so-called "own resources" — taxes and levies that are collected by EU countries but are dedicated to the EU budget, such as customs duties, a percentage of value-added taxes or a tax on non-recycled plastic waste.

The more such "own resources" the EU budget has, the less governments have to contribute from national coffers.

Costa's proposal for the digital tax builds on a 2018 proposal by the European Commission that was not taken up by EU governments at the time.

Costa has now proposed that the EU put a 3% tax on the annual net turnover from online advertising, digital intermediation services and user-generated data for companies with an annual turnover for digital activities of €50 million in the EU and a global turnover of over €750 million.

This would mean taxing mostly US-based digital giants such as Google, Microsoft, Meta, Apple or Amazon, a move many EU governments have been wary of for fear of angering US President Donald Trump, who has spoken against such a tax.

To find more money, Costa proposed slowing down the repayment of the capital of the more than €600 billion that the EU will have jointly borrowed by the end of 2026 for its post-pandemic recovery fund.

The repayment of the interest and capital will start in 2028 and last until 2058 as initially planned, but the repayment of capital may be slower in the first seven years to leave more money in the budget for other priorities, officials said.

The budget and its sources of revenue must be agreed unanimously and it is often an acrimonious battle. The seven-year ​2028-2034 budget under discussion now is particularly difficult because of additional pressures on national ⁠budgets from high energy prices and defence spending.

Although the EU budget only has to be ready for 2028, leaders want a deal by the end of 2026 because there are elections next year in France, Italy, Poland, Greece, Estonia, ⁠Finland ​and Slovakia, with the budget likely to play a role in electoral ​campaigns.

data.title: Former Italian police chief De Gennaro takes own life amid mafia probe
data.description:
Key points:
  • De Gennaro involved in probe over Borsellino bombing
  • Lawyer says investigation had deeply shaken him
  • Politicians criticise media after death

By Giulio Piovaccari and Angelo Amante

Former Italian police chief Gianni De Gennaro, under investigation for alleged efforts to obstruct a new probe into the 1992 killing of a top anti-mafia magistrate, has taken his own life, an official familiar with the matter said on Saturday.

De Gennaro, 78, served as national police chief from 2000 to 2007. One of Italy's most influential security officials, he played a key role in the fight against organised crime, particularly the campaign against Sicily's Cosa Nostra mafia in the 1980s and 1990s.

Less than a week ago, prosecutors in Caltanissetta, Sicily, named him in an investigation of alleged attempts to obstruct inquiries into a 1992 car bombing in Palermo that killed anti-mafia magistrate Paolo Borsellino and five police escorts.

A judge had rejected prosecutors' request to place him under house arrest, but they appealed and a decision was expected in the coming weeks.

News of the investigation had stunned many in Italy, including De Gennaro himself, according to people close to him. He had denied wrongdoing.

"He was deeply shaken," his lawyer Francesco Bertorotta, who had spoken to him during the week, told La Repubblica newspaper.

"He sounded distraught to me, having to defend himself against accusations he considered unjust and defamatory."

MYSTERY OF BORSELLINO INVESTIGATION

De Gennaro was found dead at his country home in Tuscany after relatives raised the alarm when they were unable to reach him, according to Italian media reports.

The handling of the investigation into Borsellino's assassination remains one of the most contentious chapters in recent Italian history. Less than two months before the killing, a mafia bomb had killed anti-mafia judge Giovanni Falcone, a close associate of De Gennaro.

Police identified suspects who were later found innocent. Subsequent investigations examined allegations that false confessions had been obtained during the inquiry.

The reasons for those developments remain disputed, and efforts are still continuing to establish the full circumstances and identify those responsible for misleading the inquiry.

The Borsellino family have repeatedly called for clarity, and reacted with dismay to news of De Gennaro's death.

"Another piece of the truth may have gone (with him)," said Manfredi Borsellino, the magistrate's son.

De Gennaro's death prompted reactions from across the political establishment. Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni expressed condolences, while some allies argued that media scrutiny had been disproportionate, given the lack of evidence against him.

"In a free, democratic and civilised country, justice is administered in courtrooms, not outside them," Deputy Prime Minister Antonio Tajani said.

DE GENNARO ROSE FROM MAFIA BATTLES TO NATIONAL PROMINENCE

De Gennaro's career spanned the battle against the Sicilian mafia and the highest ranks of Italy's police and intelligence services.

Nicknamed "The Shark", he worked closely with Falcone on landmark anti-mafia investigations and helped to oversee the extradition from Brazil of mafia informant Tommaso Buscetta.

De Gennaro later headed the Anti-Mafia Investigative Directorate, served as national police chief for seven years and subsequently led Italy's intelligence coordination department.

His career was not without controversy. As police chief, he oversaw security operations during the 2001 Group of Eight summit in Genoa, which was marred by violent clashes between police and anti-globalisation protesters.

The summit remains one of the most contentious episodes in modern Italian policing. De Gennaro consistently denied wrongdoing and was ultimately acquitted in a related case.

In 2013, he became chairman of the state-controlled aerospace and defence group Finmeccanica, later renamed Leonardo, a position he held until 2020.

data.title: Capricor reviewing operations as FDA rejects cell therapy
data.description:
Capricor Therapeutics announced that its operating expenses are under review after the U.S. Food and Drug Administration on Friday declined to approve its cell therapy candidate Deramiocel for the second time in less than two years.

In a statement, the company said the FDA issued a Complete Response Letter in connection with its resubmitted Biologics License Application for Deramiocel, rejecting the one-time therapy for Duchenne muscular dystrophy, a rare neuromuscular disorder.

The FDA attributed the decision to concerns over Deramiocel's effectiveness, among other issues. “The CRL states that the FDA does not consider the data sufficient to establish substantial evidence of effectiveness and cites certain other clinical deficiencies,” Capricor added.

The company sought U.S. approval for its lead asset after the FDA issued a complete response letter for its original BLA in July 2025. However, an independent advisory panel of the agency refused to recommend it for approval, noting that the drug lacked efficacy against cardiomyopathy in Duchenne.

Capricor shares plunged over 78% in post-market trading on Friday after the announcement.

The company reported $198.5M in cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities as of Sept. 30, which it said would be adequate to fund its operations over the next 12 months. However, given the setback, the San Diego, California-based biotech is reviewing its operating expenses to extend the cash runway.

data.title: Larry McDonald survived Lehman's collapse. Now he warns the credit market is signaling a growth shock for stocks.
data.description:
By Michael Sincere

Bear Traps Report founder explains why he sees stagflation coming, how much AI risk sits in S&P 500 index funds and why he favors hard assets

"Everybody's in growth stocks, and nobody's in value. Value stocks are going to crush growth in the coming years," says Larry McDonald.

Larry McDonald was a vice president at Lehman Brothers when the firm collapsed in 2008. Now he says he sees a record wave of convertible-bond issuance - a warning sign he saw before Lehman fell - along with a move into consumer staples and credit markets that are shutting off financing for artificial intelligence.

McDonald is the founder of "The Bear Traps Report" and the New York Times bestselling author of "A Colossal Failure of Common Sense" and "How to Listen When Markets Speak."

In this recent interview, edited for length and clarity, McDonald shares what the credit market is telling stock investors, how much AI risk sits in S&P 500 SPX index funds, which hard assets he favors, whether gold and silver are still worth buying, how investors nearing retirement can defend their portfolios and what younger investors should watch.

MarketWatch: Is there something the market is telling you that investors are missing?

McDonald: Definitely. Look at S&P [500] growth expectations for earnings next year. They're viciously high. But if you look at consumer staples (stocks of companies that sell everyday necessities, such as Walmart (WMT)) versus discretionary, consumer staples are outperforming by almost 19% in the last six months. The high-yield bond market hasn't been able to rally at all. The neoclouds (companies that rent out AI computing power) are all blowing up, and there's a big default coming there.

If you listen to the consumer staples and you listen to the bond market, all of it points to a major growth shock. That's where earnings are going to come down hard.

MarketWatch: Is the risk of a credit crisis gone, delayed or ahead of us?

McDonald: As you can see with the neoclouds, it's clearly starting again. The bulls say it's not 2000 because there's endless demand for computing power. But the only way you get endless demand is if there's endless financing and easy money. The capital markets are basically shutting off the financing for AI right now. That's what's causing the growth shock.

'The only way you get endless demand for computing power is if there's endless financing and easy money.'Larry McDonald

MarketWatch: When people buy an S&P 500 index fund, do they realize how much AI risk they are taking?

McDonald: It's pure evil. If Jack Bogle was alive right now, he would be sick to his stomach.

Ten years ago, the top two stocks in the S&P were 5% of the index. As of this month, the top two stocks are Nvidia (NVDA) and Apple (AAPL). Most investors have no idea that if they have $1 million in an S&P 500 index fund, $150,000 is in two stocks. Ten years ago, it would have been $50,000.

MarketWatch: How close is the U.S. to 1970s-style stagflation, and are investors prepared for it?

McDonald: In the '70s, that level of stagflation was a 10, which was the worst. We're not getting to that, because back then there was approximately 10% unemployment and approximately 8% inflation. But on a scale of 1 to 10, we're heading toward a 5, 6 or 7.

You don't read much about it, but everybody's in growth stocks, and nobody's in value. Value stocks are going to crush growth in the coming years. Think of the percentage of household wealth that's long hard assets, not just precious metals but copper, uranium and aluminum. In 1980, 5% or 6% of household wealth was long a lot of these commodities, and now it's less than 1%.

MarketWatch: Where would a regular investor go to buy hard assets?

McDonald: The whole AI trade for the next 20 years is going to need a lot more uranium. Sprott Physical Uranium Trust SRUUF is a really attractive commodity right now. Looking out the next three years, there's a meaningful deficit for uranium. The supply of uranium relative to global demand is going to be far short. I think that uranium prices could go up 100% to 200% in the coming years, potentially. Same thing with silver. You have a huge buildout in solar. Texas Gov.-elect Gina Hinojosa is going to do a deal with the AI infrastructure companies, the data centers, and she's going to force them into a lot more solar.

We love First Solar (FSLR). We love iShares Silver Trust SLV. With the demand for silver that's going to come from AI, and the Fed potentially having to cut off the hiking cycle and not being able to hike too much, the setup for silver and solar is extremely bullish.

MarketWatch: Gold (GC00) and silver (SI00) both hit records earlier this year, and both have since fallen sharply. Are they still worth buying?

McDonald: Silver is the industrial metal, and consumer staples have been outperforming discretionary. There's a lot of people that are worried about a slowdown. Silver's approximately 60% off the highs. That's a really bullish setup because it's already priced in a lot of the industrial pain.

On the gold side, interest on the [national] debt is $1.1 trillion, and the Fed's not going to be able to hike too much more because if they were to hike 75 basis points, interest on the debt goes to nearly $1.3 trillion. We're coming into a stagflationary environment. That's really bullish for gold.

MarketWatch: Does bitcoin (BTCUSD) belong in someone's portfolio?

McDonald: Yes. You want to track the bitcoin-gold ratio (the number of ounces of gold that one bitcoin buys). When it's in the 30s, you want to sell bitcoin and buy gold. When it gets down into 12 to 17, you want to sell some gold and buy some bitcoin.

The big problem is when you go risk-off and the VIX VIX (the market's volatility gauge) is high. Unfortunately, being long bitcoin is similar to being short the VIX. There's a lot of weak hands in bitcoin, a lot of tourists. If we go risk-off with a high VIX and the markets are down 20%, bitcoin has really suffered every time, whereas gold has been a much, much better store of value.

'Being long bitcoin is similar to being short the VIX.'Larry McDonald

MarketWatch: Over the next 12 to 24 months, what are the best opportunities that investors are overlooking?

McDonald: We love Nike (NKE) heading into the 2028 Summer Olympics. It's trading below the 200-month moving average. The capitulation score in our model was one of the greatest signals we've ever seen. If you buy Nike this far below the 200-month moving average, your probability of making money in the coming years is very, very high.

Century Aluminum (CENX) is one of our highest-conviction ideas. It's a $3 billion market cap, so it's not a big company, but we think they're going to do $1 billion of free cash flow next year. That's a 30% free-cash-flow yield. It offers investors a decent amount of protection because they're buying back stock. I think your downside is approximately 10% or 20%, but your upside is 200%.

MarketWatch: How can readers who are nearing retirement and own S&P 500 index funds defend their portfolios against a high-inflation environment?

McDonald: The first thing you want to do is call your financial adviser and have them recreate the S&P 500 with a higher weighting toward industrials, materials and energy. It should be illegal to have 50% of your S&P in tech and AI, and that's essentially where we're going to be pretty soon.

MarketWatch: Any recommendations for readers in their 20s and 30s?

McDonald: No. 1, it's a wonderful time to be a young investor because the amount of information you can get from podcasts is like reading hundreds of books. It's incredible.

I think the biggest thing for younger people is to understand how dislocated the market is historically. Whenever one sector gets too big - like in 2000, tech was too big. In 2008, financials were too big. In 2013, oil and gas were too big. Now technology (and communication services combined) is almost 45% of the S&P, and they're adding these crazy IPOs - Anthropic (ANT), OpenAI and SpaceX (SPCX). You want to always beware of when one sector gets too big, and you want to go the other way.

MarketWatch: What warning signs did you see before Lehman collapsed that investors can learn from today?

McDonald: The convertible-bond market (bonds that can be exchanged for stock) is the best leading indicator. Whenever you see an explosion of convertible-bond issuance, and we just went to a record, that means these neoclouds, there's eight of them - they have been shut out of the high-yield bond market. This is another thing we saw before Lehman and the dot-com [bust]. They've been forced into what we call the last saloon. The last saloon is the convertible-bond market.

MarketWatch: How does today compare with Lehman?

McDonald: Far more wealth is at risk to inflation and interest rates. It's a lot worse, because today, household ownership of equities is at record levels. There's a lot more wealth as a percentage of household wealth. Equities are bigger today than 2007. But when Lehman went down, bonds gave you lots of protection.

The problem today is that the deficits are so high and the irresponsibility in Washington is off the charts in terms of deficit spending that, if the stock market gets hit, the bonds aren't going to offer you the same type of protection. This could be, in a lot of ways, a lot worse than Lehman.

MarketWatch: Is there anything else you see that most investors are missing?

data.title: Indonesian Minister of Law Launches GI Tourism Indonesia, Promoting Geographical Indication Products as Tourism Attractions
data.description:
Wonosobo, Indonesia, Nov 21, 2026 - (ACN Newswire) - Minister of Law Supratman Andi Agtas officially launched GI Tourism Indonesia, or Geographical Indication Tourism, at Bukit Telaga Menjer, Wonosobo Regency, Central Java, on Wednesday (November 18, 2026). The program integrates Intellectual Property (IP) protection, particularly geographical indications, with the tourism sector to increase the economic value of regional flagship products and improve the welfare of producer communities.

"The success of geographical indications should not be measured solely by the number of certificates issued, but by the benefits genuinely experienced by the community. I believe our country has the largest number of geographical indications in the world," Supratman said at the launch of GI Tourism Indonesia, themed "A New Journey Begins in Dieng - From Origin to Experience."

According to Supratman, the time has come for the government to promote a shift in its approach to geographical indication protection, from registration to utilization, and from protection to strengthening economic value. Through GI Tourism, distinctive regional products are not merely marketed as commodities but are also presented as tourism experiences that connect visitors with the stories, culture, production processes, and communities in their places of origin.

"We want to connect legal protection with the development of economic value," he stressed.

In line with this, Deputy Minister of Tourism Ni Luh Enik Ermawati stated that current tourism trends are increasingly oriented toward seeking authentic experiences. Tourists are no longer simply looking for entertainment but also want to discover the uniqueness and stories behind the destinations they visit. According to her, Indonesia's cultural, culinary, and local product wealth represents a strength that can be developed to enhance the country's tourism appeal.

"Over time, tourist behavior has changed. In the past, people traveled simply to have fun, but now they are looking for something authentic. This is the strength of Indonesian tourism. Everything we offer in Indonesia is highly authentic," she said.

Ni Luh cited authentic tourism experiences that can be developed through cultural heritage destinations such as the Arjuna Temple Complex in Dieng, as well as gastronomic tourism that introduces not only food but also the history and culture behind it. She noted that Indonesia has approximately 6,900 tourist villages and hundreds of thousands of tourist destinations that require further development and interregional connectivity.

Therefore, collaboration across ministries and regional governments is essential. She also reported that during the 2024-2026 period, international tourist arrivals reached 12 million, representing 5 percent growth, while domestic tourist trips reached approximately 9 million, with growth of 4 percent.

Meanwhile, Director General of Intellectual Property Hermansyah Siregar explained that GI Tourism is a geographical indication-based tourism program that integrates regional specialty products with tourism experiences, production processes, local knowledge, and the culture of the communities that produce them.

"The development of GI Tourism Indonesia begins in the Dieng Area, covering Banjarnegara and Wonosobo Regencies, involving three registered Geographical Indication products: Dieng Banjarnegara Arabica Coffee, Dieng Carica, and Dieng Purwaceng," Hermansyah explained.

Hermansyah added that the Directorate General of Intellectual Property (DJKI) had carried out a series of preparations throughout 2026 to ensure that the pilot project would have a supportive ecosystem. These stages included strengthening the economic utilization of geographical indications through marketplaces, providing assistance in developing tourism concepts and packages in collaboration with the Ministry of Tourism, and enhancing community capacity through the GI Smart Preneur program.

The GI Smart Preneur activity, held on September 18, 2026, was attended by 50 participants and covered materials on strengthening substantive knowledge of geographical indications, product knowledge, storytelling skills, and tourism services.

DJKI also conducted a Familiarisation Trip on September 21-23, 2026, to test tourism routes and experiences based on the three GI products.

At the launch, DJKI also introduced the GI Tourism Expedition Book, which contains accounts of tourism experiences and digital access to learn about the products and participate in plant adoption programs in their regions of origin. One of the initiatives launched was the Dieng Purwaceng Foster Parent Movement, marked by the symbolic planting and watering of seedlings. The book is equipped with a QR code to access plant identification information and monitor documentation of their development.

A total of 80 participants are also scheduled to take part in the GI Tourism Dieng Experience to directly experience tourism based on geographical indication products, as well as the Coffee Tree Foster Parent Program alongside local farmers.

The series of activities also included the presentation of copyright recordation certificates, 10 People's Business Credit (Kredit Usaha Rakyat/KUR) facilities to MSMEs and farmers in the Dieng Mountains area, and a collective trademark registration letter for Dieng Banjarnegara Arabica Coffee.

Central Java Deputy Governor H. Taj Yasin Maimoen expressed his appreciation for the selection of the Dieng area as the location for the launch of GI Tourism Indonesia. According to him, the program marks an important moment to strengthen collaboration between Banjarnegara and Wonosobo Regencies in developing tourism potential and regional flagship products.

"On behalf of the Central Java Provincial Government, we would like to express our gratitude that Banjarnegara and Wonosobo Regencies can finally come together and collaborate for the advancement of tourism. We hope that tourism will continue to grow rapidly," he said.

Taj Yasin also expressed hope that collaboration with the Ministry of Law could be expanded to provide assistance in protecting MSME products across Central Java. He noted that many regional flagship products still have significant potential to be developed and protected through intellectual property rights.

As of November 2026, a total of 286 Geographical Indications had been registered in Indonesia, comprising 270 Indonesian GIs and 16 foreign GIs. The government is also expanding protection through international cooperation, including within the framework of the Indonesia-European Union Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (IEU-CEPA), which includes a commitment to protect 72 Indonesian GIs in the European Union.

Supratman emphasized that the development of GI Tourism must be a joint effort involving the central government, regional governments, producer communities, and business actors.

"Tourism will grow, Geographical Indication products will gain greater value, and communities in their regions of origin will become the primary beneficiaries," he concluded.

About DJKI

The Directorate General of Intellectual Property (DJKI) is an echelon I unit under the Ministry of Law of the Republic of Indonesia, tasked with formulating and implementing policies in the field of intellectual property.

DJKI provides registration and protection services for copyright, patents, trademarks, industrial designs, geographical indications, layout designs of integrated circuits, and trade secrets.

Through digital transformation and the strengthening of public services, DJKI is committed to providing fast, transparent, and accountable legal protection for all creators, inventors, and business actors in Indonesia.

data.title: Trump Pushes AI Data Centers Tax to Keep Jobs in US While Calling for Nvidia’s Jensen Huang Comeback
data.description:
The comments, made during a White House press conference on November 20, highlight two priorities for the administration: keeping artificial intelligence infrastructure within the United States and maintaining its competitive position against China.

Trump Proposes Tax on Overseas AI Data Centers

Trump said his administration would prevent American companies from establishing data centers outside the country or impose a substantial financial penalty on those that proceed. Referring to the proposed measure, he warned that companies building facilities abroad would face a “tremendous tax.”

President Trump proposed a hefty tax on US AI firms building data centers overseas to protect domestic infrastructure and jobs amid growing competition with China. Source: @SkyNews/X

“We're not going to allow our companies to build data centers outside of our country,” Trump said during the press conference.

The president argued that allowing critical technology infrastructure and manufacturing operations to move overseas could weaken America's position in the global AI race. He pointed to the semiconductor industry as an example, suggesting that the United States had fallen behind after allowing chip production to expand abroad.

The proposal reflects Trump's broader effort to attract investment, infrastructure development, and technology-related employment to the domestic market. However, he did not provide a proposed tax rate, implementation schedule, or details about which companies and projects would fall under the measure.

The announcement also came with questions about its legal and administrative feasibility. According to Axios, Trump acknowledged that he had not discussed the proposal with his officials before making the announcement. The president also did not explain whether he would seek congressional approval or attempt to use existing executive powers.

The US Constitution grants Congress authority to impose federal taxes, leaving the precise legal route for Trump's proposed measure unresolved. No formal legislative framework or implementing regulations were outlined during the announcement.

Domestic Data Center Expansion Faces Public Opposition

Trump's proposal comes as the rapid expansion of AI infrastructure faces growing resistance in several US communities. Although the administration wants companies to build more facilities domestically, the projects have generated concerns about electricity consumption, water requirements, and their potential impact on household utility costs.

Data centers require substantial computing capacity to train and operate increasingly sophisticated AI models. Their electricity demand can place additional pressure on local power networks, while cooling systems can require significant water resources. These issues have become prominent subjects in local planning discussions and election campaigns.

The backlash also became a political issue during the 2026 midterm election cycle, with voters considering measures to restrict or impose additional conditions on data center development. Consequently, Trump's effort to discourage overseas construction comes at a time when some American communities are questioning the costs of hosting these facilities.

There is also an economic consideration. Data center operators frequently establish facilities close to customers to reduce processing delays and the expense of transmitting large volumes of information. For companies serving international clients, maintaining infrastructure across different countries can therefore remain important.

A policy that increases the cost of overseas construction could influence future investment decisions by US technology firms. However, its ultimate impact would depend on the scope of the proposed tax and whether companies receive any exemptions.

Trump Highlights AI Competition With China

Trump linked his data center proposal to the wider competition between Washington and Beijing over artificial intelligence. During the same press conference, he discussed his recent Asia trip and his conversations with Chinese President Xi Jinping.

Morgan Stanley is projecting capacity to climb from 48 GW in 2026 to 117 GW by 2030. Source: @MojoTricks/X

The president claimed that he and Xi had agreed to establish “joint guardrails” for AI development. He did not explain what those safeguards would involve or whether they would lead to any formal agreement between the two governments.

Trump also described artificial intelligence as “super intelligence,” arguing that the United States remained ahead of China in the race to develop the technology. He presented the competition as largely revolving around the two countries, with China occupying second place in his assessment.

The comments come amid continuing US efforts to restrict China's access to advanced computing technology. The Commerce Department has moved to tighten controls on advanced AI chip exports to several Southeast Asian countries to prevent the technology from reaching Chinese companies through third-party channels.

Data centers have become part of this broader technology competition because they allow businesses to access powerful processors and computing resources without necessarily purchasing the hardware themselves. Reuters has reported that Chinese companies have continued accessing computing capacity through overseas data centers in countries permitted to receive advanced chips.

This creates a connection between Trump's proposed tax and the administration's semiconductor policies. Both approaches seek to protect America's technological position while limiting the channels through which China can access advanced AI computing resources.

Trump Calls for Jensen Huang's Return to Nvidia

Alongside his comments about AI infrastructure, Trump renewed his support for Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia chief executive.

Huang resigned from his positions as president, CEO, and board member on November 12, 2026, following reports involving alleged extramarital relationships. Nvidia's board subsequently appointed Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress as interim CEO while beginning the search for a permanent replacement.

President Trump called on Nvidia’s board to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO, urging it to accept his apology and give him another opportunity. Source: @wallstengine/X

Trump described Huang as one of the most talented figures in the technology industry and argued that Nvidia should consider giving him another opportunity to lead the company.

“I would love to see him back,” Trump said, adding that Huang should “be given a second chance.”

The president also suggested that Nvidia should accept an apology from its former chief executive and allow him to return to work. He credited Huang with helping develop the company's advanced Blackwell AI chip platform, which has become an important part of its computing business.

Trump further argued that Huang's technical contributions had helped put the United States significantly ahead in AI chip development. His remarks reflected concern about losing an executive whose work has been closely associated with Nvidia's expansion in the global semiconductor industry.

The comments followed an earlier wave of support for Huang from technology industry figures and investors. Elon Musk and Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney were among those who backed a petition calling for Nvidia to reconsider the decision while an independent investigation proceeds.

Nvidia Board Maintains Leadership Transition

Despite Trump's public backing, Huang's return to Nvidia does not appear to be part of the board's current plans. The Associated Press reported that a person familiar with the board's thinking said directors were not considering reinstating the former CEO.

The circumstances surrounding Huang's resignation remain sensitive. Reports described alleged relationships with a senior Nvidia executive who reported to him and a Chinese businesswoman suspected by US intelligence of having connections to Beijing. The latter allegation has not been publicly established as fact, and Trump has questioned whether the woman was a spy.

The issue has also raised questions about corporate governance, executive conduct, and potential national security concerns. Nvidia's board now faces the task of maintaining confidence among investors, employees, and customers while the company searches for permanent leadership.

The administration itself has shown differing views on the company's future. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent previously called for a significant leadership shake-up and suggested that Nvidia should consider an external candidate. Trump's endorsement of Huang's return therefore contrasts with Bessent's stated preference for a different leadership direction.

For now, Colette Kress remains responsible for Nvidia's executive leadership while the board considers potential successors. The company has said it expects operations, customer commitments, and its product roadmap to continue without interruption.

Trump's two announcements highlight the administration's growing focus on the strategic importance of AI infrastructure and semiconductor leadership. However, the proposed overseas data center tax still lacks an implementation framework, while Huang's potential return depends on a decision by Nvidia's board rather than presidential support alone.

data.title: LMT Gets $740M Awards, GD, RTX Pick Up Missile Contracts – A Look At This Week’s Defense Deals
data.description:
Key points:
  • Lockheed Martin secured around $740 million in defense awards related to F-35 fighter jets and C-5 transport aircraft.
  • General Dynamics and RTX picked up additional military contracts for Stryker armored vehicles and rolling airframe missiles
  • Elbit Systems reported a 17% increase in Q3 revenue to $2.25 billion, while order backlog reached $33 billion.

Defense contractors were in focus this week as Lockheed Martin (LMT), General Dynamics (GD) and RTX (RTX) secured new multi-million-dollar contracts, while Elbit Systems (ESLT) reported topline growth in the third quarter.

The U.S. Navy also selected 28 companies for an electronic-warfare program with a combined contract ceiling exceeding $7.1 billion.

Lockheed Martin Picks Up $740M In Defense Awards

Lockheed Martin received a $330.6 million Navy contract modification on Thursday for materials and components needed to produce 75 F-35 Lightning II fighter jets for the U.S. military. A day earlier, the company secured a $316.6 million Air Force contract for logistics and maintenance support for C-5 Galaxy transport aircraft.

That followed a $93.2 million Navy order on Tuesday for F-35 maintenance and sustainment, including cybersecurity upgrades and specialized repair capabilities.

The three deals carried a combined value of roughly $740 million.

General Dynamics, RTX Add To Contract Wins

General Dynamics secured a $332.5 million Army contract on Wednesday for maintenance, training and other support services for its Stryker armored vehicles. Its Mission Systems unit also received a $20.5 million Navy modification deal on Tuesday for submarine combat-system software.

Meanwhile, RTX’s Raytheon unit received a $120.3 million Navy modification award on Thursday to produce Rolling Airframe Missiles for the U.S. Navy. That followed a separate $12.3 million modification contract for engineering and technical support on the missile system.

Separately, Elbit Systems reported third-quarter (Q3) revenue of $2.25 billion Tuesday, up 17% year over year but marginally below Street estimates, according to Fiscal.ai. Earnings per share rose to $4.36 from $3.35, while its order backlog climbed to $33 billion.

Navy Names 28 Contractors For $7.1B Program

On Thursday, the Navy announced a $7.13 billion multiple-award contract under its Surface Electronic Warfare Improvement Program, which helps warships detect and counter enemy threats.

Recipients include Lockheed Martin, General Dynamics, RTX, Northrop Grumman (NOC), Leidos (LDOS), CACI International (CACI), HII (HII), Amentum (AMTM) and Frequency Electronics (FEIM).

Despite the contract wins, shares of Lockheed Martin, General Dynamics, RTX and Elbit Systems fell 5.1%, 4.24%, 2.45% and 1.45%, respectively, this week.

data.title: From ChatGPT to Claude deals: Walmart looks like an agentic AI winner
data.description:
Walmart developed its generative AI shopping assistant Sparky to very little fanfare as part of a broader push into what it called adaptive retail. While early buzz was light, the payoff for Walmart investing in Sparky is just beginning.

CEO John Furner noted that in Walmart's third quarter, U.S. usage of Sparky climbed 129% year over year, with baskets associated with the assistant running 40% larger. The AI assistant helps shoppers discover items, plan meals, summarize reviews, turn photos of handwritten lists into carts, and reorder staples based on inventory positioning, pricing, and delivery speed.

Walmart began its efforts to scale generative AI across customers, members, associates, and partners in 2024. The retail giant introduced Sparky in June 2025 inside its app and web experience, pairing text chat with voice and image inputs. Rather than relying on a single bot for everything, Walmart structured its AI ecosystem around specialized agents, separating shopping discovery in Sparky from dedicated customer-support automation that handles order lookup, returns, and delivery updates. The company also expanded beyond proprietary surfaces by partnering earlier this year with OpenAI to bring Sparky into ChatGPT and building a Google Gemini shopping experience.

Meanwhile, Anthropic partnered with Walmart to help power Sparky itself using Claude models such as Claude Sonnet 4.6. On the consumer side, rather than embedding a standalone Sparky widget inside Claude, Walmart opened its Agent Gateway, built on Anthropic's Model Context Protocol, in October. This allows approved third-party assistants, including Claude, to search Walmart's catalog and prepare orders directly on a shopper's behalf using user-controlled Agent Profiles and spending limits.

Looking ahead, Walmart plans to scale Sparky across more markets, languages, and shopping modes while building infrastructure for third-party AI agents. It has already rolled Sparky out in the U.S., Canada, Mexico, and Sam's Club with support for languages such as Spanish and French. Next, Walmart is introducing Agent Profiles so shoppers can set permissions, spending limits, track agent purchases separately, or revoke access, alongside a Walmart Agent Gateway to govern how approved external agents interact with its catalog.
